newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Unrelenting sales push Nigerian shares lower.
newsitem.headline: Unrelenting sales push Nigerian shares lower.

text.p: Unrelenting sales of blue chip shares continued on the Nigerian stock exchange on Monday, forcing prices lower, dealers said.
The all-share index closed down at 8308.12 from 8329.18 on Friday.
Dealers said the difficult economic environment was forcing investors to sell.
"People are still selling to cut their losses because they believe the shares are going to fall further," one dealer said.
Another said blue chips were losing their appeal because investors were moving into lower-priced stocks in the hope of hedging possible losses.
Petroleum marketer Mobil fell on Monday because of fears it would soon follow other companies in the sector and report a poor full year result, traders said.
"The main reason for its slide today was lack of information. The full year result is due but they are not forthcoming with it," said Chuks Ohanwunsi, a trader with Networth Securities and Finance.
The stock closed 50 kobo lower at 64.50 naira the same price as Unipetrol which also slid 50 kobo.
Others in the sector also fell. Agip at 15.20 naira, Total at 55.90 naira and National Oil at 50.30 naira all dropped 30 kobo.
Food companies were also down. Flour Mills ended 10 kobo down at 15.90 naira. Cadbury fell 20 kobo to 34.80 naira. Nestle was 10 kobo down at 51.40 naira.
Traders raised AIICO Insurance by 10 kobo to 14.80 naira because of its favourable full year result.
Speculation saw healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham climb 20 kobo to 5.20 naira.
Brewer Guinness rose 10 kobo to 8.35 naira and construction firm Cappa and D'Alberto ended 20 kobo up at 13.20 naira.
